findings.title: Logout and login startup have no timeout
findings.description:
D7 sets timeouts for only three things: `thread.run`, `handle.wait()`, and runtime start plus `account()`. Two other runtime calls have no limit:
- **`sq auth logout`** spawns the runtime and calls `AsyncCodex.logout()` (lines 82, 84). If the runtime hangs here, the command hangs forever. No failure mode is listed for a logout hang, a failed runtime start, or the transport closing during logout.
- **`sq auth login`** has a gap before the wait. `codex.login_timeout_s` covers only `handle.wait()`. Runtime spawn, `initialize`, and `login_chatgpt()` / `login_chatgpt_device_code()` all run before it with no limit. A runtime that hangs during startup blocks login with no timeout message.

This breaks the project rule that every new I/O path lists its hang, timeout and disconnect cases. Fix: add rows for login startup and for logout. Put a limit on both, for example by reusing `codex.account_timeout_s` for runtime start plus `logout()` and for the startup step of login. State the exit code and message for each.

findings.title: After a turn timeout, it is unclear whether the client is reused or reset
findings.description:
Line 82 says each `CodexAgent` keeps one lazy client and reuses it for every later message. Line 129 says that when the transport closes, `_codex`/`_thread` are cleared so a dead client is not reused. The timeout rows (125, 128) say the turn is cancelled and "`shutdown()` still runs in `finally`". That leaves two readings:
- If `shutdown()` runs in the `finally` of each `handle_message`, it contradicts the reuse on line 82. It also leaves `_codex` pointing at a closed client unless state is cleared, and line 125 does not say it is.
- If `shutdown()` runs only when the agent is shut down, then after a timeout the next message reuses a thread whose cancelled turn may still be running in the runtime.

Fix: give the timeout and cancellation rows the same reset as the transport-closed row (shut down the client and clear `_codex`/`_thread`). Say which `finally` is meant.

findings.title: The SDK version bound contradicts itself and does not protect a fast-moving 0.x SDK
findings.description:
D1 sets `openai-codex>=0.159.3,<1`. Special Considerations (line 231) says the upper bound "is not decided here" and that the SDK's "generated surface moves". Those two statements conflict. Also, for a 0.x package whose API keeps changing, `<1` allows every future 0.x release, so it protects almost nothing. A user who installs `[codex]` later can pull in an SDK where `TurnResult`, `TurnStatus` or the login handles have changed. The real-types test (line 200) only catches this for the version CI happens to install.

Fix: pick a bound that matches the stated risk, such as `~=0.159.3` or `<0.160`, with a note on how to raise it. Or justify `<1` explicitly. Then remove the contradiction on line 231.

findings.title: A strategy named as generic becomes Codex-specific
findings.description:
Slice 128 renamed `CodexAuthStrategy` to `OAuthFileStrategy` and the auth type `"codex"` to `"oauth"`, on the grounds that the name "describes mechanism, not product" (128 slice, line 181 and line 225). This design makes `OAuthFileStrategy` implement `InteractiveLogin` by driving `AsyncCodex.login_chatgpt()` (lines 66-67). As a result, any future profile with `auth_type = "oauth"` would get the Codex ChatGPT login. That is the hidden product coupling the rename was meant to remove. The design does reject profile-name dispatch, correctly, but it moves the coupling into the auth-type registry instead.

Fix: either state that `"oauth"`/`OAuthFileStrategy` now means the Codex runtime's file store, and record the narrowing, or put the login on a Codex-specific strategy, for example a subclass registered under its own auth type. Without this, the "capability, not a profile check" goal in D3 is only partly met.

findings.title: The `--timeout` flag duplicates the config key
findings.description: `codex.login_timeout_s` already makes the login timeout configurable. A second override through `sq auth login --timeout` adds another surface, another precedence rule and more tests, and no stated requirement asks for it. Consider cutting the flag. Likewise, `codex.account_timeout_s` could be a constant in `config/keys.py` instead of a user setting.

findings.title: The slice plan entry lists fewer dependencies than the design needs
findings.description: The frontmatter correctly adds slice 931 (`applies_effort`, `core/usage.py`, the `ProviderError.telemetry` field). The slice plan entry (`100-slices.orchestration-v2.md:79`) still lists only `[128]`. Update the plan so the ordering is visible there.

findings.title: Interfaces Required leaves out SDK types the design depends on
findings.description:
D8 and the failure table use several SDK types that are not in the Interfaces Required list:
- `TurnResult.status`, `TurnStatus`, `TurnResult.error.message`
- `CodexError`
- `TransportClosedError`, `ServerBusyError`, `RetryLimitExceededError`, `CodexRpcError`

Listing them would make the real-types drift test's coverage explicit.

findings.title: The design hedges a distribution name that is already known
findings.description: `pyproject.toml` already declares `name = "squadron-ai"`. The "(or the equivalent for the project's published name)" on line 25 and "confirmed … during implementation" on line 171 can be removed, so the single hint constant is fixed in the design.

findings.title: Whether Codex failures carry usage data is not stated
findings.description: Under slice 931's D12, a `ProviderError` leaving `handle_message` carries `telemetry` for the provider-failure artifact. The field is optional and defaults to `None`, so leaving it out is valid. One sentence saying Codex failures carry `telemetry=None` (or the last turn's usage, if any) would make the failure artifact's contents explicit.
